paper_title: Before Generation, Align it! A Novel and Effective Strategy for   Mitigating Hallucinations in Text-to-SQL Generation
caption: Results of different schema linking modules on BIRD-dev.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the performance of three different schema linking modules—DIN-SQL (zero-shot), TA-SQL (zero-shot), and DIN-SQL (few-shot)—on the BIRD-dev dataset, measured by three evaluation metrics: Recall, Precision, and F1 Score. The horizontal axis displays the three metrics in order: Recall, Precision, and F1 Score, while the vertical axis represents the score values on a linear scale ranging from 40 to 100, with tick marks at intervals of 20. For each metric, three bars are grouped together, each corresponding to one of the three models, as indicated by the legend: light blue for DIN-SQL (zero-shot), dark blue for TA-SQL (zero-shot), and light green for DIN-SQL (few-shot). In Recall, the scores are 63.58 (DIN-SQL zero-shot), 71.90 (TA-SQL zero-shot), and 72.29 (DIN-SQL few-shot). For Precision, the scores are 88.89, 91.24, and 92.31, respectively. In F1 Score, the values are 75.34, 80.40, and 81.08. The bars are arranged in ascending order of metric from left to right, and each bar is labeled with its exact numerical value. The chart visually shows that DIN-SQL (few-shot) consistently achieves the highest scores across all three metrics, followed by TA-SQL (zero-shot), with DIN-SQL (zero-shot) performing the lowest in each case.
